pm_structure.summary: Group-level construct: the Board Investment Committee approves Investment Policy Statements and guidelines; portfolios appear to be run through external investment managers (FS cite 'investment managers' as valuation sources and a payable 'due to the investment manager'), with Wawanesa Life itself acting as investment manager of its segregated funds. No in-house asset-management affiliate.
manager_entities: External investment managers (not named in FS)
Wawanesa Life (manager/administrator of its own segregated funds, C$7.3mm fees 2025)
bullets: Investment Policy Statement sets maximum equity levels and credit limits; approved by Investment Committee of the Board (quarterly credit and interest-rate reporting)
Equities held largely via pooled funds (common stocks/pooled funds C$232mm); fixed income C$1.02bn, ~A-rated average (AAA 120, AA 293, A 366, BBB balance)
Securities lending run through the custodian's program (custodian guarantee, daily mark-to-market over-collateralisation)
Assets invested to match liability cash flows by segment (par vs non-par); interest-rate risk monitored by management and Board Investment Committee
Group ESG: PRI signatory, PCAF member (Jul 2026); impact-investment goal 10% of P&C and Life portfolios by 2030 (6% at YE2025)

rotation_commentary.text: Common stocks rose to C$232mm from C$189mm (market gains; minimal purchases) while fixed income edged down to C$1.02bn; equities now ~19% of invested assets.
Group: 'investments are managed in a conservative manner'; sustainable/impact allocation 6% of enterprise portfolio vs 10% target by 2030; Scope 3 financed-emissions target -25% by 2030.
Fixed-income book is long: C$1.56bn of C$1.92bn undiscounted FI cash flows fall beyond five years (duration-matched to life liabilities).

securities_lending.text: Fixed-income securities on loan with fair value C$112.9mm (2024: C$143.8mm), via custodian program; collateral exceeds loan value, marked daily; cash collateral reinvested in custodian's Common Investment Account

repos.text: No repurchase or reverse repurchase agreements disclosed

structured_indirect.text: No derivatives, CLO/ABS, mortgages, private credit, fund finance or sidecar exposure disclosed; portfolio is public fixed income plus pooled-fund equities (no Level 3 assets)
Reinsurance: reinsurance contract held assets C$171.1mm; catastrophe cover for group business

deals.text: Group: acquired Everest Insurance Company of Canada (announced Mar 23 2026, closed Oct 1 2026; ~C$305mm commercial premiums, +30%); rebranded WSI, A Wawanesa Company
Group: sold Wawanesa General Insurance Company (US) to the Automobile Club of Southern California (closed Mar 31 2024; net proceeds US$89.9mm, gain C$53.3mm); no remaining foreign operations
Related-party distribution: Western Financial Group (group broker) earned C$4.6mm commissions from Wawanesa Life and placed C$40.9mm of Life premiums

notes: Small, unlevered, plain-vanilla life subsidiary of a large P&C mutual: C$2.0bn assets (26% seg funds), C$1.26bn general account that is 81% public fixed income and 19% pooled-fund equities, no derivatives, no debt, LICAT 167%. The only balance-sheet 'leverage' item is C$113mm of securities on loan through the custodian. Group context matters for the deck: Wawanesa Mutual (C$12.5bn assets, equity C$5.5bn, MCT 290%) sold its US P&C arm to AAA in 2024 and bought Everest Canada in Oct 2026.
